title: Rama eliminates Maareecha
introduction: Rama eliminates Maareecha when he is escaping beyond reach in the form of Golden Deer. He sports with that deer for a long time and when it is leading him away and afar from the hermitage, he is vexed with the trickery of the deer and kills it. At the time of his death Maareecha shouts out for Seetha and Lakshmana, as demanded by Ravana. Rama is perplexed at this oddity of Maareecha and presumes that some danger is immanent and then returns to hermitage.
closing: As with any other demon's death Maareecha's death also is eulogised as a merited one and reading or listening this is said to bring merit. Though these results are not said in Ramayana proper, its collateral scripts like skānda purana, ādhyātma rāmāyaṇaetc., say them. For the elimination of Maareecha ādhyātma rāmāyaṇasays:

From that body of Maareecha a divine aureole risen while all the world is seeing... that merged into Rama alone, causing very great astonishment... this is the marvel of Rama, nothing else..' So the divine beings thought seeing from heavens, and said 'a Brahman or a demon, or a sinner or meritorious one who cites the name of Rama at the time of leaving his body, he attains the Ultimate Threshold...' Blessing so, the divine beings returned to their abodes on seeing the salvation of Maareecha's soul in Rama.' ādhyātma rāmāyaṇa, aranya, seventh sarga/chapter.
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे चतुः चत्वारिंशः सर्गः

verses.devanagari:
तथा तु तम् समादिश्य भ्रातरम् रघुनंदनः |
बबन्ध असिम् महातेजा जांबूनदमयः त्सरुम्
verses.iast:
tathā tu tam samādiśya bhrātaram raghunaṃdanaḥ |
babandha asim mahātejā jāmbūnadamayaḥ tsarum
verses.translation: Rama, the great-resplendent scion of Raghu, on instructing his brother Lakshmana in that way securely fastened his sword with golden handle to his waist.

glosses.meaning: highly resplendent, Raghu's, scion of - Rama

verses.devanagari:
ततः त्रि विनतम् चापम् आदाय आत्म विभूषणम् |
आबध्य च कलापौ द्वौ जगाम उदग्र विक्रमः
verses.iast:
tataḥ tri vinatam cāpam ādāya ātma vibhūṣaṇam |
ābadhya ca kalāpau dvau jagāma udagra vikramaḥ
verses.translation: Rama whose valour is escalating then took his own insignia, the three-way arched bow called kodanDa, and fastened two quivers and proceeded.

glosses.meaning: one with - up, risen - escalating, valour - Rama

verses.devanagari:
तम् वंचयानो राजेन्द्रम् आपतन्तम् निरीक्ष्य वै |
बभूव अंतर्हितः त्रासात् पुनः संदर्शने अभवत्
बद्ध असिः धनुः आदाय प्रदुद्राव यतो मृगः |
verses.iast:
tam vaṃcayāno rājendram āpatantam nirīkṣya vai |
babhūva aṃtarhitaḥ trāsāt punaḥ sandarśane abhavat
baddha asiḥ dhanuḥ ādāya pradudrāva yato mṛgaḥ |
verses.translation: On peering at the peerless one among kings, namely Rama, who is indeed coming down on him, that Golden Deer disappeared as if with fear and even to beguile him, and again it came into clear visibility. And Rama speedily spurted to that place from where the Golden Deer has firstly disappeared with securely grit sword and firmly handled bow.

glosses.meaning: who is coming, falling - coming down on it
[securely] grit, sword, bow, on taking [firmly handled]

verses.devanagari:
तम् स्म पश्यति रूपेण द्योतमानम् इव अग्रतः
अवेक्ष्य अवेक्ष्य धावन्तम् धनुष् पाणिः महावने |
अतिवृत्तम् इषोः पातात् लोभयानम् कदाचन
शंकितम् तु समुद् भ्रान्तम् उत्पतन्तम् इव अंबरे |
दृअश्यमानम् अदृश्यम् च वन उद्देशेषु केषुचित्
चिन्न अभ्रैः इव संवीतम् शारदम् चन्द्र मण्डलम् |
verses.iast:
tam sma paśyati rūpeṇa dyotamānam iva agrataḥ
avekṣya avekṣya dhāvantam dhanuṣ pāṇiḥ mahāvane |
ativṛttam iṣoḥ pātāt lobhayānam kadācana
śaṃkitam tu samud bhrāntam utpatantam iva ambare |
dṛaśyamānam adṛśyam ca vana uddeśeṣu keṣucit
cinna abhraiḥ iva saṃvītam śāradam candra maṇḍalam |
verses.translation: Rama the wielder of bow kept on beholding that Golden Deer which is observing him over and over and running away into deep of the forest. In the next moment he has seen it right in front of him as though effulgent with its marvellous form. At times he has seen it running away as though to circumvent the fall of arrow, and at times stopping only to tantalise him. Sometimes it appeared to be springing as though to skies in very highly perplexity of wariness. It is disappearing somewhere in the thickets of forest, and it is putting in an appearance elsewhere in those thickets, like the autumnal orb of the moon under the fly front of splintered clouds.

glosses.meaning: on observing, on observing - deer repeatedly observing the hunter, Rama
in deep, forest, running away, that - deer
beholding, he [the hunter] remained - kept on

verses.devanagari:
मुहूर्तात् एव ददृशे मुहुर् दूरात् प्रकाशते
दर्शन अदर्शनेन एव सः अपाकर्षत राघवम् |
सुदूरम् आश्रमस्य अस्य मारिचो मृगताम् गतः
verses.iast:
muhūrtāt eva dadṛśe muhur dūrāt prakāśate
darśana adarśanena eva saḥ apākarṣata rāghavam |
sudūram āśramasya asya mārico mṛgatām gataḥ
verses.translation: In a wink Rama could proximately see that Maareecha who transformed himself into the Golden Deer, and again in a flash he appeared distantly. Thus that deer/demon has drawn off Raghava very far from his hermitage in this hide and seek game.

glosses.meaning: deer-hood, who went into - who is animalised
for a moment, thus - in a wink
by revealing, not, revealing [concealing himself, hide and seek game] only
to side, attracted - sidetracked, drawn off.

verses.devanagari:
आसीत् क्रुद्धः तु काकुत्स्थो विवशः तेन मोहितः |
अथ अवतस्थे सुश्रान्तः च्छायाम् आश्रित्य शाद्वले
verses.iast:
āsīt kruddhaḥ tu kākutstho vivaśaḥ tena mohitaḥ |
atha avatasthe suśrāntaḥ cchāyām āśritya śādvale
verses.translation: Rama of Kakutstha is incensed as its form is spellbinding but its capture slippery, and then verily tired as he is he stayed on a pasture taking shelter of a tree shade.

glosses.meaning: by its [form,] spellbound, kaakutsthaH tu = Kakutstha, but
kutuuhala paravashaH = 1]out of, control - slippery, 2] fascinated
shade [of tree,] taking shelter, on pasture, he stayed on.

verses.devanagari:
स तम् उन्मादयामास मृगरूपो निशाचर |
मृगैः परिवृतो अथ वन्यैः अदूरात् प्रत्यदृश्यत
verses.iast:
sa tam unmādayāmāsa mṛgarūpo niśācara |
mṛgaiḥ parivṛto atha vanyaiḥ adūrāt pratyadṛśyata
verses.translation: Nightwalker Maareecha has further maddened Rama in the guise of Golden Deer by reappearing in his close-by, surrounded with other animals of the forest.

glosses.meaning: in guise, he that Maareecha, night-walker

verses.devanagari:
ग्रहीतु कामम् दृष्ट्वा तम् पुनः एव अभ्यधावत |
तत् क्षणात् एव संत्रासात् पुनर् अंतर्हितो अभवत्
verses.iast:
grahītu kāmam dṛṣṭvā tam punaḥ eva abhyadhāvata |
tat kśaṇāt eva santrāsāt punar aṃtarhito abhavat
verses.translation: Again on seeing Rama who is stalking his catch that deer ran towards him as though to impress with its guilelessness, and just at that moment it vanished again as if with extreme fear.

glosses.meaning: to catch, desirous of - he who is stalking
at him - at Rama on seeing

verses.devanagari:
पुनर् एव ततो दूरात् वृक्ष खण्डात् विनिःसृतः |
दृष्ट्वा रामो महातेजाः तम् हन्तुम् कृत निश्चयः
verses.iast:
punar eva tato dūrāt vṛkśa khaṇḍāt viniḥsṛtaḥ |
dṛṣṭvā rāmo mahātejāḥ tam hantum kṛta niścayaḥ
verses.translation: Then that deer has again emerged out of the thick of trees, and on spotting it the great-resplendent Rama has firmed up his decision to fell it.

glosses.meaning: to kill, firmed up, his decision.

verses.devanagari:
भूयः तु शरम् उद्धृत्य कुपितः तत्र राघवः |
सूर्य रश्मि प्रतीकाशम् ज्वलंतम् अरि मर्दनम्
संधाय सुदृढे चापे विकृष्य बलवत् बली |
तम् एव मृगम् उद्दिश्य श्वसंतम् इव पन्नगम्
मुमोच ज्वलितम् दीप्तम् अस्त्रम् ब्रह्म विनिर्मितम् |
verses.iast:
bhūyaḥ tu śaram uddhṛtya kupitaḥ tatra rāghavaḥ |
sūrya raśmi pratīkāśam jvalaṃtam ari mardanam
saṃdhāya sudṛḍhe cāpe vikṛṣya balavat balī |
tam eva mṛgam uddiśya śvasaṃtam iva pannagam
mumoca jvalitam dīptam astram brahma vinirmitam |
verses.translation: At that instant Raghava became highly infuriated and unholstered a holocaustic, enemy-subjugating arrow that is similar to the flare of the sun, tautening it on his very sturdy bow that forceful Rama forcefully outstretched the bowstring with arrow targeting the Golden Deer alone, and released that fierily blazing arrow-missile which is carefully created by Brahma and which is hissing like a snake.

glosses.meaning: very, sturdy, in bow, tautened, taking aim
that, deer, only, on aiming - on targeting

verses.devanagari:
शरीरम् मृग रूपस्य विनिर्भिद्य शरोत्तमः
मारीचस्य एव हृदयम् विभेद अशनि संनिभः |
verses.iast:
śarīram mṛga rūpasya vinirbhidya śarottamaḥ
mārīcasya eva hṛdayam vibheda aśani saṃnibhaḥ |
verses.translation: On very profoundly impaling the body of deer's form that superb arrow which is similar to a thunderbolt has severed the heart of Maareecha in the core of deer's body.

verses.devanagari:
ताल मात्रम् अथ उत्प्लुत्य न्यपतत् स भृश आतुरः
व्यनदत् भैरवम् नादम् धरण्याम् अल्प जीवितः |
verses.iast:
tāla mātram atha utplutya nyapatat sa bhṛśa āturaḥ
vyanadat bhairavam nādam dharaṇyām alpa jīvitaḥ |
verses.translation: Then Maareecha is highly frenzied as his lifespan is minimised, blared a blaring shriek, vaulted up to a height of palm-tree, and fell down onto the ground.

verses.devanagari:
म्रियमाणः तु मारीचो जहौ ताम् कृत्रिमाम् तनुम्
स्मृत्वा तत् वचनम् रक्षो दध्यौ केन तु लक्ष्मणम् |
इह प्रस्थापयेत् सीता ताम् शून्ये रावणे हरेत्
verses.iast:
mriyamāṇaḥ tu mārīco jahau tām kṛtrimām tanum
smṛtvā tat vacanam rakśo dadhyau kena tu lakśmaṇam |
iha prasthāpayet sītā tām śūnye rāvaṇe haret
verses.translation: Maareecha on his part abandoned the body of Golden Deer when he is dying. But remembering the words of Ravana that demon gave a thought, 'how best will Seetha hasten Lakshmana to this place, and how best Ravana can abduct Seetha in a place void of people.'
notes: Maareecha would have died without yelling for Lakshmana or Seetha as tutored by Ravana because Maareecha is no real alley of Ravana. But it is said that he 'recollected Ravana's words and thought about it.' What he really thought is the causation of death to that one who caused his own death, namely Ravana. Ravana can do nothing to Maareecha now as Maareecha is breathing his last. Whatever is to be done now it has t become a self-ruinous act to Ravana. Hence, it is better to do as said by Ravana for the elimination of Ravana. So thought Maareecha.

glosses.meaning: when dyeing, on his part, Maareecha
by what, Lakshmana, will be hastening

verses.devanagari:
स प्राप्त कालम् अज्ञाय चकार च ततः स्वरम् |
सदृशम् राघवस्य एव हा सीते लक्ष्मण इति च
verses.iast:
sa prāpta kālam aGYāya cakāra ca tataḥ svaram |
sadṛśam rāghavasya eva hā sīte lakṣmaṇa iti ca
verses.translation: Perceptive of the time that chanced bearing his death, and wishful of the death of Ravana too, then made a voice that is a soundalike to Raghava's voice and yelled 'ha, Seetha...' also thus 'ha Lakshmana...'

verses.devanagari:
तेन मर्मणि निर्विद्धम् शरेण अनुपमेन हि |
मृग रूपम् तु तत् त्यक्त्वा राक्षसम् रूपम् आस्थितः
चक्रे स सुमहा कायम् मारीचो जीवितम् त्यजन् |
verses.iast:
tena marmaṇi nirviddham śareṇa anupamena hi |
mṛga rūpam tu tat tyaktvā rākṣasam rūpam āsthitaḥ
cakre sa sumahā kāyam mārīco jīvitam tyajan |
verses.translation: When Rama's incomparable arrow has indeed shattered his crucial organ, namely the heart, in a downright manner, then Maareecha assumed a very massive physique of a demon, abandoning the form of Golden Deer.
notes: Though Maareecha assumed the form of a deer he has to retain his heart and brain of a demon. This is the yogic way of para kāya praveśanam 'entering other bodies.' These assumed artificial bodies do not hold ground in nidrā, surata, maraṇa daśeṣu 'in sleep, copulation and death states,' where the mind, if distracted to these states, cannot concentrate or hold the body that is assumed by mental powers of yoga. Here no supernal god or deity is involved to grant such a capacity but one's own practise achieves it. Whereas in other case like Ravana, gods have bestowed boons, so he need not practise such yoga etc., as he is blessed to be above these mortal's practises and thus can change his form and can rejoice in any state with that body or form. This is how he abducts Seetha changing his semblances instantaneously.

glosses.meaning: that, deer's, form, but, on abandoning

verses.devanagari:
तम् दृष्ट्वा पतितम् भूमौ राक्षसम् भीम दर्शनम्
रामो रुधिर सिक्त अंगम् चेष्टमानम् महीतले |
जगाम मनसा सीताम् लक्ष्मणस्य वचः स्मरन्
verses.iast:
tam dṛṣṭvā patitam bhūmau rākṣasam bhīma darśanam
rāmo rudhira sikta aṃgam ceṣṭamānam mahītale |
jagāma manasā sītām lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ smaran
verses.translation: On seeing that demon with a fiendish look, who has fallen to earth with limbs steeped in blood, and who is weltering on the surface of earth, Rama emotionally took flight to Seetha reminiscing Lakshmana's words.

glosses.meaning: to Seetha, by heart, went - emotionally took flight to Seetha.

verses.devanagari:
मारीचस्य तु माय एषा पूर्व उक्तम् लक्ष्मणेन तु |
तत् तदा हि अभवत् च अद्य मारीचो अयम् मया हतः
verses.iast:
mārīcasya tu māya eṣā pūrva uktam lakśmaṇena tu |
tat tadā hi abhavat ca adya mārīco ayam mayā hataḥ
verses.translation: "This is the trickery of Maareecha which Lakshmana vouchsafed earlier, that has indeed happened in that way alone, and the one whom I have killed now is none other than Maareecha.

verses.devanagari:
हा सीते लक्ष्मण इति एवम् आक्रुश्य तु महा स्वनम् |
ममार राक्षसः सो अयम् श्रुत्वा सीता कथम् भवेत्
लक्ष्मणः च महाबाहुः काम् अवस्थाम् गमिष्यति |
इति संचिन्त्य धर्माअत्मा रामो हृष्ट तनू रुहः
verses.iast:
hā sīte lakṣmaṇa iti evam ākruśya tu mahā svanam |
mamāra rākṣasaḥ so ayam śrutvā sītā katham bhavet
lakṣmaṇaḥ ca mahābāhuḥ kām avasthām gamiṣyati |
iti sañcintya dharmāatmā rāmo hṛṣṭa tanū ruhaḥ
verses.translation: "This demon died while crying out with a blatant voice 'ha, Seetha... ha, Lakshmana...' And on hearing this how Seetha will be? And what will be the plight of dextrous Lakshmana?" Thus on thinking over them that righteous-souled Rama remained in a hair-raising predicament.

glosses.meaning: on hearing, Seetha, how, she will be

verses.devanagari:
तत्र रामम् भयम् तीव्रम् आविवेश विषादजम् |
राक्षसम् मृग रूपम् तम् हत्वा श्रुत्वा च तत् स्वनम्
verses.iast:
tatra rāmam bhayam tīvram āviveśa viṣādajam |
rākṣasam mṛga rūpam tam hatvā śrutvā ca tat svanam
verses.translation: On killing that demon in the form of Golden Deer, and also on hearing his yelling, Rama is ensorcelled with a frantic fear caused by his own gloom.

glosses.meaning: in deer's, form, that, demon, on killing
his, yelling [of demon,] on hearing, also

verses.devanagari:
निहत्य पृषतम् च अन्यम् मांसम् आदाय राघवः |
त्वरमाणो जनस्थानम् ससार अभिमुखः तदा
verses.iast:
nihatya pṛṣatam ca anyam māṃsam ādāya rāghavaḥ |
tvaramāṇo janasthānam sasāra abhimukhaḥ tadā
verses.translation: Raghava then on killing another spotted deer and on taking its flesh, he hurried himself towards Janasthaana.

glosses.meaning: to Janasthaana, towards, he drifted, proceeded.
